note: United States: All 63 national parks with a full guide, and 4,994 more places on the map: other NPS units from the NPS Data API; every state park from PAD-US; every national forest, grassland and wildlife refuge, the BLM's monuments and conservation areas, National Natural Landmarks and scenic byways from their agencies' own data. Guide prose is written for Unigrids; descriptions, fees, hours, visitor centres and photographs are the NPS's own; places with no agency prose carry a lead adapted from Wikipedia, credited where it is shown. Japan: all 35 national parks with a guide, their areas and designation years from the Ministry of the Environment's national park table, outlines from its zone file and 2024 visitors from its statistics; and 58 quasi-national parks from the Ministry's list, outlined from OpenStreetMap where it maps them and otherwise shown as a point, with leads adapted from Wikipedia. Prefectures from Natural Earth; huts and rail from OpenStreetMap; photographs from Wikimedia Commons, credited individually. Norway: all 48 national parks with a guide, 195 landscape protection areas and 230 nature reserves of 10 km² or more, from Miljødirektoratet's Naturvernområder (NLOD 2.0; outlines simplified by Unigrids) and Kartverket's counties (CC BY 4.0). Guide prose is written for Unigrids; huts, rail lines and stations are from OpenStreetMap (ODbL); photographs are from Wikimedia Commons, each with its own credit and licence; places without a guide carry a lead adapted from Wikipedia where one exists, credited where it is shown. New Zealand: all 13 national parks with a guide and 49 conservation and forest parks of 5 km² or more, from the Department of Conservation's Public Conservation Land (CC BY 4.0, Crown Copyright: Department of Conservation Te Papa Atawhai; outlines simplified by Unigrids) and Stats NZ's regions (CC BY 4.0). Huts, campsites, visitor centres and tracks are DOC's own (CC BY 4.0); rail lines and stations are from OpenStreetMap (ODbL). Guide prose is written for Unigrids; photographs are from Wikimedia Commons, each with its own credit and licence; places without a guide carry a lead adapted from Wikipedia where one exists, credited where it is shown. Unigrids is not affiliated with DOC and carries no DOC logo. Canada: all 48 national parks and national park reserves and Rouge National Urban Park with a guide, 5 national marine conservation areas, and 254 provincial and territorial parks of 100 km² or more, from the Canadian Protected and Conserved Areas Database (Environment and Climate Change Canada; outlines simplified by Unigrids). Trails, campgrounds, huts, visitor centres and attendance are Parks Canada's own; all of these are used under the Open Government Licence – Canada. Rail lines, stations and other huts are from OpenStreetMap (ODbL). Guide prose is written for Unigrids; photographs are from Wikimedia Commons, each with its own credit and licence; places without a guide carry a lead adapted from Wikipedia where one exists, credited where it is shown. Unigrids is not affiliated with Parks Canada and carries neither its beaver symbol nor its wordmark. Australia: 51 national parks with a guide — the Commonwealth's six and the state parks in a World Heritage property or named their state's flagship — and 666 other state and territory national parks, from the Collaborative Australian Protected Areas Database 2024 (© Commonwealth of Australia, DCCEEW, CC BY 4.0; outlines simplified by Unigrids) and the ABS's states and territories (CC BY 4.0). Queensland's walking tracks and their grades are the Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service's (© State of Queensland, CC BY 4.0); other trails, rail lines, stations, visitor centres, campgrounds and huts are from OpenStreetMap (ODbL). Guide prose is written for Unigrids; photographs are from Wikimedia Commons, each with its own credit and licence; places without a guide carry a lead adapted from Wikipedia where one exists, credited where it is shown. Unigrids is not affiliated with Parks Australia or any state or territory park agency and carries none of their logos.
